question: Can a learned correction of the detector's foot point bring our player positions near the truth (now 0.9-1.4 m off)?
status: exploratory, CPU, written before any fit (owner, 2026-10-26)
data: the shots clips with pitch tracks (.cache/gpu/<w>/output_<w>/metric_v3s_link.parquet), every 10th frame; all matches but M1 (its truth boxes are in another frame); M7 / M9 through src/unseal.py
pairs: player detections matched to truth persons by feet (eval_soccertrack_v2.match_feet, 43 px)
target: the image offset from the detection's foot point (px_raw, py_raw) to the truth box's bottom centre
model: sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor per offset component, features: u, v, box height, box width, height/width, image width; defaults
validation: leave one match out; error = pitch distance (release calibration) to the truth's pitch position, median and p90, before vs after, per held-out match and pooled
adopt if: pooled held-out median error falls by >= 30% and no held-out match gets worse
